articles.headline: BJP set to gain Rajya Sabha seat in upcoming biennial elections
articles.summary: The Election Commission announced biennial elections for 10 Rajya Sabha vacancies in Uttar Pradesh, one in Uttarakhand, and a bypoll in West Bengal on October 16. The BJP, currently holding 116 seats, is expected to gain one seat. The Samajwadi Party is projected to win two seats, while the Bahujan Samaj Party faces losing its entire presence in the Upper House.

articles.headline: Supreme Court asks Election Commission to clarify voter roll revision notices
articles.summary: The Supreme Court directed the Election Commission to address voter concerns regarding 3.3 million notices issued during Delhi's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The court questioned if notices were sent mechanically and asked for clarity on 'logical discrepancies.' It emphasized that citizens should not face penal consequences for conscientious objections.

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders Uttar Pradesh to replace Lakhimpur Kheri trial prosecutor
articles.summary: The Supreme Court directed the Uttar Pradesh government to replace the public prosecutor in the 2021 Lakhimpur Kheri violence trial against Ashish Mishra. The decision followed reports that crucial witnesses were being dropped. While dismissing a plea to remove the presiding officer, the court asked the Allahabad High Court to monitor allegations of witness intimidation.

articles.headline: Minor girl gang-raped by three men posing as police in Delhi
articles.summary: A 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three men inside Delhi's Aastha Kunj park on Monday evening. The suspects, posing as police, threatened the victim and her friend with a firearm and knife. Three men have been arrested. The incident highlights security lapses in the Capital, including non-functional CCTVs and poor lighting in the 142-acre park.

articles.headline: Two main suspects arrested after encounter in Bihar molestation case
articles.summary: Bihar police arrested two primary suspects in the alleged harassment and molestation of minor students in Jamui district following an encounter on Tuesday. One suspect sustained a bullet injury, while another was injured while fleeing. Five individuals, including three minors, have now been held in connection with the incident, which came to light through a viral video.

articles.headline: India approves Asad Alam Siam as new Bangladesh High Commissioner
articles.summary: India formally approved the appointment of Bangladesh Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam as the next High Commissioner to New Delhi. Siam, a career diplomat who joined the service in 1995, will replace Riaz Hamidullah in the coming weeks. The move comes as both nations seek to reset bilateral relations following recent political transitions in Bangladesh.

articles.headline: Teenager dies by suicide in Jhansi after alleged gang-rape and threats
articles.summary: A 19-year-old woman died by suicide in Uttar Pradesh's Jhansi after being allegedly gang-raped by six people, including three minors. The victim's family claimed the suspects threatened to circulate a video of the crime. Police have apprehended five of the six accused and are investigating the circumstances leading to the woman's death on Tuesday morning.

articles.headline: Governance concerns raised over Tata Sons chairman's family ties with TVS
articles.summary: Documents revealed that family members of Tata Sons chairman N. Chandrasekaran hold business relations with TVS Motor Co. Ltd. The relationship, involving a warehouse project, was reportedly not disclosed to the Tata Sons board or Tata Trusts. This revelation has deepened the rift within India's largest conglomerate as leadership performance remains under review.

articles.headline: India joins EU and others to launch platform for multilateralism
articles.summary: India joined the European Union, Australia, Brazil, and Canada to launch the 'Partners for Multilateralism, International Law, Peace and Prosperity' (P4M) platform. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar emphasized the need for participative deliberations and transparent decision-making at the UN General Assembly, noting that the global order is currently under stress.

articles.headline: CPWD orders vacation of Shastri and Krishi Bhawans for new construction
articles.summary: The Central Public Works Department (CPWD) directed government departments to hand over Shastri Bhawan and Krishi Bhawan by the end of September. The move paves the way for the construction of Kartavya Bhawan 4 and 5 in Central Delhi. The project, part of the Central Vista redevelopment, is estimated to cost approximately ₹3,155.41 crore.

articles.headline: Environment Ministry extends validity of port project clearances to 20 years
articles.summary: The Union Environment Ministry extended the validity of environmental clearances for ports, harbours, and dredging projects from 10 to 20 years. The move aims to improve the ease of doing business and rationalizes validity for projects with high gestation periods. This aligns port project clearance timelines with those currently granted to mining projects.

articles.headline: India wins first gold medal at Asian Games in women's cricket
articles.summary: The Indian women's cricket team clinched the nation's first gold medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games by defeating Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final. Smriti Mandhana top-scored with 79, and Shafali Verma contributed 48 as India posted 216/3. Sri Lanka was bundled out for 69. This victory marks India's third consecutive major multi-nation final win over Sri Lanka.

articles.headline: India narrowly defeats Japan by two runs in rain-curtailed T20I
articles.summary: India secured a two-run victory over Japan in a rain-curtailed one-off T20 match reduced to five overs. India managed only 32/4 on a turning surface, but Axar Patel's disciplined bowling restricted Japan to 30. The narrow victory against the world's 41st-ranked team came in a historic encounter celebrating 75 years of diplomatic ties between the two nations.

articles.headline: Trump confirms meeting between US and Iranian officials at UN
articles.summary: President Donald Trump stated that US and Iranian officials met on Tuesday during the UN General Assembly. The meeting occurred shortly after Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran if a deal to end the seven-month war is not reached. While describing the meeting as 'very good,' Trump emphasized he has a major decision to make regarding the future of the conflict.

articles.headline: Data shows 53 student deaths at IITs over last five years
articles.summary: Official data reveals that at least 53 students died across various IITs between 2020-21 and 2024-25. More than half of the deaths involved students from SC, ST, and OBC categories. The figures, which include 45 suicides, highlight concerns over academic pressure and mental health. The government has reminded institutions to report all such incidents immediately to the police.

articles.headline: Delhi government plans new think tank for state development plans
articles.summary: The Delhi government prepared a cabinet note to establish the Delhi Institute for Transformation and Innovation (DITI). Modeled after the Centre's NITI Aayog, the think tank will frame long-term development plans, including a 'Vision Delhi 2047' document. The initiative aims to help the state government frame detailed development plans and promote innovation.

articles.headline: NDMC introduces mandatory four-way waste segregation and steep fines
articles.summary: The New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) framed new waste management bylaws for Lutyens' Delhi. The rules mandate four-way waste segregation at the source and impose steep fines for sanitation violations. The civic body is also reworking monthly user charges as part of efforts to modernize waste management and improve environmental standards in the area.

articles.headline: India condemns Pakistani air strikes on Afghan border regions
articles.summary: India criticized Pakistan's air strikes on Afghan border areas in Kunar and Paktika provinces, which resulted in civilian casualties. The Ministry of External Affairs termed the acts as 'aggression' that vitiates regional peace and security. The statement aligns with New Delhi's consistent stance of backing Kabul during flare-ups of regional tensions.

articles.headline: JPMorgan CEO urges US not to penalize India over Russian oil
articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co Chairman Jamie Dimon stated that the US should not punish India or global oil markets for purchasing Russian crude. In an interview, Dimon highlighted the technical challenges refiners face in switching supplies. He cautioned against disrupting global energy markets while attempting to pressure Russia to end its war in Ukraine.

articles.headline: Princess Diana's brother makes damning allegations against King Charles
articles.summary: Charles Spencer, the Earl of Spencer, released a book titled 'Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,' accusing King Charles III of having 'contempt' for the late Princess. The book claims Charles was 'elated' after her death and argued against his sons walking behind the funeral procession. Buckingham Palace issued a rare response, suggesting grief may have clouded the Earl's memory.

articles.headline: DGCA initiates financial and operational scrutiny of SpiceJet
articles.summary: Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu announced that the DGCA is conducting operational and financial scrutiny of SpiceJet following frequent flight delays and cancellations. The airline's domestic market share fell to 1.6% in July. The government aims to ensure no lapses in safety while monitoring the airline's financial health and passenger service stability.

articles.headline: Angel One founder buys Juhu luxury tower for record ₹711 crore
articles.summary: Dinesh Thakkar, founder of Angel One, purchased an eight-storey sea-facing tower in Mumbai's Juhu for ₹711 crore. The 63,000 square foot property represents the most expensive single residential unit purchase in India. The deal highlights the continued demand for luxury high-end real estate in Mumbai's upscale neighborhoods.

articles.headline: India's Russian oil imports drop 16.5% as West Asian supplies rise
articles.summary: India's share of Russian oil imports fell by 16.5% in August to 2.1 million barrels per day. The decline coincided with increased supplies from the Middle East, particularly the UAE. Refiners are tapping spot markets amid fears of potential US tariffs on Russian oil and geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, though Russia remains India's top supplier.

articles.headline: India rejects Pakistan's attempt to involve UNSC in Indus Waters dispute
articles.summary: India dismissed Pakistan's effort to bring a Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling regarding the Indus Waters Treaty to the UN Security Council. New Delhi described the move as 'malicious propaganda' and reiterated that it does not recognize the 'illegally constituted' court in The Hague. India maintain its decision to hold the treaty in abeyance remains in force.

articles.headline: Drought conditions affect 52.5% of India as monsoon ends
articles.summary: The India Drought Monitor reports that 52.5% of the country is in a drought category due to a 15% rainfall deficit as the monsoon concludes. Maharashtra, Telangana, and Karnataka are severely affected, with soybean and paddy crops facing significant stress. While irrigation coverage has improved to 60%, farmers in rain-dependent regions expect lower yields.

articles.headline: CID investigation reveals massive question leak in KPSC recruitment
articles.summary: A CID probe into Karnataka Public Service Commission veterinary officer recruitment found that 60 to 80 questions were leaked to candidates. Investigators traced a money trail of ₹1.52 crore and arrested several individuals, including a former controller of examinations. The High Court has ordered a fresh Special Investigation Team to conduct a de novo probe into the case.

articles.headline: Karnataka Assembly unanimously rejects draft ESA notification for Western Ghats
articles.summary: The Karnataka Assembly passed a resolution rejecting the Centre's proposal to declare 20,668 sq km of the Western Ghats as an Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA). The state requested a one-year extension to conduct physical surveys and address livelihood concerns. The resolution opposes the 'unscientific' demarcation based on satellite data rather than survey numbers.

articles.headline: Karnataka launches action plan to reduce population salt consumption
articles.summary: Karnataka Health Minister U.T. Khader launched the 'State Multisectoral Action Plan for Salt Reduction' to promote healthier dietary habits. Indians consume 8-11 grams of salt daily, nearly double the WHO recommendation. A Technical Advisory Group will provide guidance on reducing salt intake to prevent non-communicable diseases like hypertension and cardiovascular issues.

articles.headline: Prime Minister unveils logo for birth centenary of Pejavara Swami
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled the logo for the birth centenary celebrations of the late Padma Vibhushan Sri Vishwesha Tirtha Swami of Udupi. Meeting with Sri Vishwaprasanna Tirtha Swamiji in New Delhi, the PM praised the late seer's life of devotion and service. Various initiatives are planned to carry forward his ideals during the upcoming centenary year.

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders fresh SIT probe into Dharmasthala rape-murder
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ordered a new Special Investigation Team to probe the 2012 Dharmasthala rape and murder case after DNA evidence revealed hair samples from unknown individuals on the victim's clothing. The court criticized previous investigations for failing to examine key witnesses. The new SIT, headed by a senior officer, has three months to complete the investigation.

articles.headline: Opposition claims Karnataka faces financial crisis alongside severe drought
articles.summary: Leader of Opposition R. Ashoka alleged that Karnataka is suffering from a 'financial drought' as it exhausts its borrowing capacity while dealing with a natural drought. Ashoka claimed the state lacks funds for relief measures and that pending bills across departments stand at ₹36,136 crore. He criticized the government for failing to take precautionary relief measures.

articles.headline: Kerala government orders bribery inquiry against CM Vijayan and family
articles.summary: The Kerala government ordered a police inquiry into allegations of bribery involving Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter Veena T, and son-in-law P.A. Mohammed Riyas. The probe follows an Enforcement Directorate report alleging kickbacks from Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited. The CPI(M) has alleged a political conspiracy between the Congress and BJP.

articles.headline: Former employee arrested in connection with granite baron's Pocso case
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu police arrested a former employee of granite baron R. Veeramani for possessing a video showing the industrialist acting inappropriately with a minor. The suspect, Ganeshan, allegedly failed to report the video and was involved in property sales that helped Veeramani evade arrest. The arrest is part of a broader investigation into sexual crimes and financial transactions.

articles.headline: Man arrested for setting woman on fire at Tiruvallur hospital
articles.summary: A 35-year-old man, Prakash, was arrested for allegedly throwing petrol on a 26-year-old woman and setting her ablaze at a government hospital in Tiruvallur, Tamil Nadu. The victim suffered 50% burn injuries. Prakash was apprehended after a police encounter in which he was shot in the leg. Authorities are investigating the motive behind the attack.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu expands school breakfast scheme to benefit 1.5 million students
articles.summary: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay launched the expanded 'Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme,' now covering students in Classes 6 to 8 in government schools. The initiative aims to benefit 1.53 million additional students across 15,454 schools with a total outlay of ₹724 crore. The launch included interactions with students and a breakfast event in Chennai.

articles.headline: Hyderabad police hunt for man after girlfriend found dead in hotel
articles.summary: Police in Hyderabad are searching for Srinivasa Ravi Teja, who allegedly absconded after bringing his girlfriend's body to a hospital. The couple had checked into a hotel in Madhapur where signs of injury and bloodstains were found. The victim, Sharon Nikhitha Topno, had head and face injuries. A murder case has been registered as police track the suspect's movements.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh on high alert as Cyclone Arnab approaches coast
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government stepped up preparedness as a depression in the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into Cyclone Arnab. Heavy to very heavy rainfall and winds up to 60 kmph are predicted for north-coastal districts on September 24. Control rooms have been established, and schools in Srikakulam were closed as authorities prepare for potential landfall.

articles.headline: Prime Minister to chair brainstorming session with Union ministers
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will chair a two-day 'Chintan Shivir' starting Wednesday to review the performance of Union ministries. The session will focus on assessing targets, outcomes, and strategizing for the remainder of the government's third term. Eight ministerial groups will present on themes like administrative success and communication to improve governance.

articles.headline: Congress alleges BJP orchestrated attack on leaders during Assam bypoll
articles.summary: The Congress party alleged that BJP workers attacked the convoy of senior leaders, including Bhupesh Baghel and Gaurav Gogoi, during a bypoll campaign in Nagaon, Assam. Stones and bottles were reportedly hurled at vehicles amid black-flag protests. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma dismissed the claims, calling it a clash between rival Congress factions.

articles.headline: Bombay High Court warns Vijay Mallya over social media posts
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court cautioned businessman Vijay Mallya against sharing documents from his pending criminal case on social media. The warning came after the Enforcement Directorate objected to Mallya posting their court affidavit on X. The court is hearing Mallya's plea to close criminal proceedings and directed SBI to file a fresh affidavit in the matter.

articles.headline: Amit Shah sets 2029 deadline to eradicate drug trade in India
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah declared a target to eliminate the drug trade in India by December 31, 2029. Speaking at a conference of anti-narcotics task forces, Shah emphasized moving from 'meeting to mission' mode. He launched a Vision Document for 2026-29, which includes a roadmap for intelligence, investigation, and financial action against narcotics networks.

articles.headline: Allahabad High Court cautions retail chain over Santa cap mandate
articles.summary: The Allahabad High Court observed that compelling employees of different faiths to wear Santa Claus caps at the workplace could hurt religious sentiments. The court warned a retail chain management in Agra after a supervisor allegedly forced subordinates to wear the caps. It emphasized that citizens in a democracy are free to follow their own faith and beliefs.

articles.headline: New governance framework under Article 371 proposed for Ladakh
articles.summary: Ladakh Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra announced that a new governance model under Article 371 is being developed to provide specific constitutional safeguards for the Union Territory. The Home Ministry is scheduling meetings with local groups to discuss the model. The framework aims to address the administrative and political aspirations unique to the Ladakh region.

articles.headline: Fire in Adilabad hospital newborn unit kills three infants
articles.summary: Three newborns died after a fire broke out in the Special Newborn Care Unit of the RIMS hospital in Adilabad, Telangana. The fire, allegedly caused by an air-conditioning unit explosion, affected 24 infants in the ward. While one baby died at the spot, two others succumbed during treatment. Chief Minister Revanth Reddy ordered an inquiry into the tragic incident.

articles.headline: Man kills wife and two priests in Azamgarh shooting
articles.summary: A man in Azamgarh, Uttar Pradesh, allegedly shot and killed his wife and two priests during a religious ceremony at his home. The suspect, Arvind Singh, reportedly opened fire after an argument regarding the priests' identification cards. Following the killings, Singh locked himself in a room with his children. Police are conducting rescue efforts and attempting to apprehend him.

articles.headline: Kazakh coach booked for allegedly raping minor cyclist at NIS Patiala
articles.summary: A cycling coach from Kazakhstan was booked for the alleged rape of a 16-year-old national-level cyclist at the National Institute of Sports in Patiala. The incident reportedly occurred on September 13 in the coach's residential quarters. Police have seized the suspect's passport and issued a lookout circular after he fled the premises. Special teams are conducting raids.

articles.headline: American citizen Matthew VanDyke seeks discharge in immigration case
articles.summary: US citizen Matthew Aaron VanDyke, charged with violating the Immigration and Foreigners Act, paid ₹5.5 lakh in compounding charges before seeking discharge from court. He was arrested by the NIA for allegedly training ethnic armed groups in Myanmar. While granted default bail, the NIA continues to investigate broader conspiracy charges under the UAPA.

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses challenge to SC/ST Act arrest provisions
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed a petition challenging the constitutional validity of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The court maintained that existing safeguards in previous rulings are sufficient to prevent misuse. It emphasized that while individual cases of misuse can be reviewed, the bar on anticipatory bail remains valid.

articles.headline: ED charges former Chhattisgarh PSC chairman in recruitment scam
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate filed a prosecution complaint against former CGPSC chairman Taman Singh Sonwani and six others in a money laundering case. The charges involve alleged corruption and question paper leaks in recruitment exams held in 2020 and 2021. The agency claims Sonwani entered a criminal conspiracy to facilitate the selection of favored candidates.

articles.headline: IAF expects technical issues of LCA Mk-1A to be resolved shortly
articles.summary: IAF Vice Chief Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit stated that technical issues delaying the delivery of the LCA Mk-1A fighter jet should be fixed within two months. The delays were primarily due to engine supply issues and radar integration. Once resolved, the aircraft will be inducted. India is also preparing for the Tarang Shakti multilateral air combat exercise in Jodhpur.

articles.headline: Supreme Court questions massive price disparity in cancer medicines
articles.summary: The Supreme Court criticized a 10-fold disparity in the pricing of essential cancer drugs, where medicines sold to retailers for ₹2,700 reach consumers at ₹27,000. Describing the situation as 'broad daylight dacoity,' the court questioned why authorities had failed to regulate prices. It sought a response from the government on mechanisms to make generic medicines affordable.

articles.headline: President Murmu presents 72nd National Film Awards in Gujarat
articles.summary: President Droupadi Murmu presented the 72nd National Film Awards in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat. Veteran actor Anant Nag received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award. Films like 'Amaran', 'Kalki 2898 AD', and 'Article 370' were recognized across various categories. The President urged the industry to promote healthy lifestyles and be mindful of their influence on young audiences.

articles.headline: Five Adani Group companies settle Sebi probe for ₹1.5 crore
articles.summary: Five Adani Group companies settled regulatory proceedings with Sebi regarding alleged disclosure lapses and audit compliance issues by paying ₹1.5 crore. The settlement follows investigations triggered by the Hindenburg Report. While the firms resolved the case through the settlement mechanism, they did so without admitting or denying the allegations of professional standards violations.

articles.headline: White House launches 24/7 streaming platform 'Trump TV'
articles.summary: The White House launched 'Trump TV,' a 24/7 streaming service featuring presidential speeches, announcements, and updates. The platform aims to provide a dedicated channel for administration content. The launch occurs amid tensions between the Trump administration and news organizations over revoked press credentials and restricted access to White House events.

articles.headline: UN report warns of potential loss of human control over AI
articles.summary: A UN independent scientific panel warned that current AI training methods could lead to a 'loss of control' by humans. The report highlighted risks of autonomous agents adopting their own goals or concealing actions. Experts called for global AI governance and updated safeguards to ensure systems remain under human direction as their capabilities rapidly evolve.

articles.headline: Student shooter injures 11 at high school in Turkey
articles.summary: A 15-year-old student opened fire outside a high school in Manisa, Turkey, wounding at least 11 pupils. Two victims are in critical condition. The assailant was arrested, and his parents and grandfather—who owned the weapon—were detained by authorities. The incident has raised concerns over school safety and weapon accessibility in the region.

articles.headline: Indian men's badminton team secures medal at Asian Games
articles.summary: The Indian men's badminton team defeated hosts Japan 3-0 in the quarter-finals of the Asian Games, guaranteeing at least a bronze medal. Lakshya Sen won a dramatic three-game opener, followed by a doubles victory by Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty. Ayush Shetty sealed the win, setting up a semi-final clash against China.

articles.headline: Wushu athlete Roshibina Devi Naorem assures India of medal
articles.summary: Wushu player Roshibina Devi Naorem secured a medal for India by reaching the semi-finals of the women's 60kg category at the Asian Games. She defeated Chu Man Sin of Macau in the quarter-finals. Roshibina, who previously won silver and bronze in earlier editions, remains a strong contender as the competition progresses.

articles.headline: China's absence in 49kg category boosts Mirabai Chanu's medal hopes
articles.summary: Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu's prospects for an Asian Games medal increased after China decided not to field athletes in the women's 49kg division. Her primary rival is now two-time defending champion Ri Song Gum of North Korea. Chanu, an Olympic silver medalist, is reported to be in peak physical condition ahead of her competition on Wednesday.
